title: Weight gets slightly smaller higher above Earth
summary: Because gravity weakens with distance from Earth's center, an object weighs a little less high above the surface.
body: NASA Glenn's beginners' guide says weight decreases with altitude because surface gravity depends on the square of the distance from Earth's center. In the page's example, a model rocket that weighs 100 pounds at the surface weighs about 99.65 pounds at 35,000 feet, a loss of about 0.35 pounds. The page presents that as a small change. It is a worked example in a guide last updated 20 November 2023, not a measurement of one particular rocket.

sources.title: Weight Equation
sources.author: Nancy Hall, NASA Glenn Research Center
sources.note: Public-domain NASA Glenn page, last updated 20 November 2023. Paraphrase of the altitude example: 100 pounds at the surface and about 99.65 pounds at 35,000 feet.
